text:
ana: quick design review — timepicker keyboard nav & sampling microcopy. I pushed a quick variant in figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/latency-dash?node-id=42. PTAL, mainly worried about keyboard flow and the 'sampling' language.

kevin: :eyes: nice. For p95 card, can we switch label from 'p95' to '95th percentile (latency)'? New people get confused.

sam: Heatmap color bins look ok but legend needs counts. When sample rate changes the distribution shifts — users should see a small 'estimated' badge.

ryan: Are we planning to default sampling ON for wide ranges? Need to be careful: could hide spikes in small windows.

a11y-bot: Keyboard nav notes: timepicker needs roving tabindex, focus outline 3px, high contrast. Also add aria-live region for streaming value updates.

ana: Proposed microcopy options: 1) 'Sampling: estimated – actual values shown on zoom' 2) 'Sampled view — rates may be approximate' 3) 'Estimated sample rate (click for details)'. Which reads best?

kevin: Leaning to #3. Also add a tooltip '? Estimated sample rate' that shows actual ratio and last computed time.

sam: code suggestion for focus:
```
.selector:focus { outline: 3px solid #0b66ff; box-shadow: none; }
```
Also need a visually-hidden label for screen readers on the sampling toggle.

ryan: UX question: if I zoom after we auto-sample, do we auto-refresh to unsampled full data? I'd expect zoom -> fetch full data for that range.

ana: yes — proposed behavior: zoom -> auto-switch to full fetch for < 30m ranges, keep sampling badge but change wording to 'full data'. I'll update figma and add dev notes. Assigning @kevin for handoff. Thanks all :tada:
